name: E-Commerce Defective Smartphone Refund Denial
raw_input: I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on an e-commerce app on 10th November 2024. It was delivered on 14th November. Within 24 hours of opening the box, the screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working. I raised a replacement request on 15th November. The app sent a technician for inspection on 21st November. The technician confirmed it is a manufacturing hardware defect and took sign on his job sheet. But on 23rd November, customer support cancelled my return request stating 'The 7-day return window expired on 21st November'. They are telling me to go to an authorized brand service center 40 km away. I paid for a brand new working phone, not a defective phone repaired on day one. I have the invoice, delivery receipt, technician inspection job sheet copy, and chat screenshots.

case_dossier.case_title: Defective Smartphone Delivery and Refused Replacement
case_dossier.summary: The complainant purchased a Samsung Galaxy smartphone for Rs 26,999, which arrived with a manufacturing defect. Although a technician verified the defect within the return window, customer support later cancelled the replacement request claiming the return window expired.

timeline.event: Ordered Samsung Galaxy smartphone on the e-commerce app.
Screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working.
Raised a replacement request on the app.
Technician inspected the device, confirmed the manufacturing hardware defect, and took a signature on the job sheet.
Customer support cancelled the return request stating the 7-day return window expired on 21st November.

evidence_needed: Written emails sent to customer support
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong documentary proof including invoice, delivery receipt, and an official technician job sheet confirming the manufacturing defect.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: Your consumer rights are fully protected under Indian law, as you reported a manufacturing defect within the permitted timeframe and possess an official technician's verification. Under the Consumer Protection Act, supplying a defective product and refusing to refund or replace it constitutes both a 'defect in goods' and an 'unfair trade practice'. Your immediate takeaway is that you have strong documentary evidence (invoice, job sheet, chats) to challenge the e-commerce platform's unfair refusal of your replacement.

governing_laws.relevance: Protects you as a consumer who bought goods for consideration through an online e-commerce transaction.
Defines a 'defect' as any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, or standard required under a contract.
Classifies refusing to refund or replace defective goods within the stipulated or reasonable period as an 'unfair trade practice'.
Establishes product manufacturer and seller liability for manufacturing and design defects.

action_options.title: Immediate Pre-Litigation Action (Formal Legal Notice / Helpline)
action_options.details: Lodge a formal grievance on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) toll-free at 1915 or via consumerhelpline.gov.in. Additionally, serve a formal Legal Demand Notice to the seller and e-commerce platform highlighting the technician's job sheet and your timely reporting.

action_options.title: Statutory Authority / Grievance Portal Filing
action_options.details: File an electronic consumer complaint online on e-Daakhil (edaakhil.nic.in) attaching your order invoice, defect photos, technician job sheet, and communication history. Note: DLSA Helpline 15100 provides free legal aid and guidance only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings.

action_options.title: Statutory Forum / Consumer Commission Petition
action_options.details: If the pre-litigation notice and NCH escalation do not yield a replacement or refund, pursue a formal consumer complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You do not need a physical advocate to file a consumer complaint. Consumer Commissions in India are designed for self-representation, allowing citizens to file and argue their cases personally without mandatory legal representation.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE**

**BY SPEED POST WITH ACKNOWLEDGEMENT DUE / REGISTERED EMAIL**

**Date:** 08/11/2026

**To,** 
The Grievance Officer / Authorized Representative, 
[E-Commerce Platform / Seller Name], 
[Company Address Line 1], 
[Company Address Line 2], 
City - [Pincode]. 

---

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR SUPPLYING DEFECTIVE GOODS, UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICES, AND WRONGFUL REFUSAL OF REPLACEMENT REGARDING ORDER OF SAMSUNG GALAXY SMARTPHONE (AMOUNT: RS. 26,999).**

---

Sir / Madam,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my client, **[Complainant's Name]**, residing at [Complainant's Address] (hereinafter referred to as the **"Client"**), I do hereby serve upon you this formal Legal Demand Notice under the relevant provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, on account of supplying a defective product and subsequently engaging in unfair trade practices by refusing a valid replacement, and state as under:

### **1. RECITALS & FACTUAL SEQUENCE**

1.1. That on **10th November 2024**, the Client placed an online order for a Samsung Galaxy smartphone through your e-commerce platform/application, paying a valuable consideration of **Rs. 26,999** [Payment transaction details / Receipt Reference if applicable]. 
1.2. That the said smartphone was delivered to the Client on **14th November 2024**. 
1.3. That **within 24 hours of delivery**, the smartphone exhibited severe hardware defects—specifically, the screen started flickering with green lines and touch functionality completely stopped working. 
1.4. That acting promptly and within the permissible return/replacement window, the Client raised a formal replacement request on your application on **15th November 2024**. 
1.5. That on **21st November 2024**, an authorized technician visited the Client, thoroughly inspected the device, physically verified and confirmed the manufacturing hardware defect, and obtained the Client's signature on the official inspection job sheet. 
1.6. That despite the official verification by your authorized technician, your customer support arbitrarily and wrongfully cancelled the return request on **23rd November 2024**, falsely alleging that the 7-day return window had supposedly expired on 21st November 2024, completely ignoring the fact that the request was raised well within time on 15th November 2024.

---

### **2. VIOLATION OF STATUTORY PROVISIONS**

Your aforesaid acts of delivering a defective product and subsequently refusing a legitimate replacement by raising arbitrary procedural technicalities constitute direct violations of the consumer rights protected under the **Consumer Protection Act, 2019**:

* **Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:** Protects the Client as a consumer who bought goods for consideration through an online e-commerce transaction.
* **Section 2(10) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:** Defines a "defect" as any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, or standard required under a contract. The delivered Samsung Galaxy smartphone suffered from a direct manufacturing hardware defect.
* **Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:** Classifies refusing to refund or replace defective goods within the stipulated or reasonable period as an "unfair trade practice."
* **Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:** Establishes product manufacturer and seller liability for manufacturing and design defects.

---

### **3. DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION**

In light of the above facts and statutory provisions, you are hereby called upon to:

1. **Process and deliver a brand-new, defect-free replacement** of the Samsung Galaxy smartphone, OR in the alternative, **issue a complete refund of Rs. 26,999** directly to the Client's original payment source; and
2. Confirm compliance with this demand within a strict **15-day rectification demand window** from the date of receipt of this notice.

---

### **4. WARNING OF FURTHER LEGAL ACTION**

Please take notice that if you fail to comply with the demands outlined above within the stipulated **15-day period**, my client shall be constrained to initiate appropriate legal proceedings against your entity without any further reference. 

These proceedings will include filing a formal consumer complaint before the appropriate **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission**, seeking a full refund/replacement, compensation for mental agony, and litigation costs. Additionally, the matter shall be escalated to the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) via 1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in. 

*(Note: For free legal guidance and information regarding consumer rights, citizens may contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline at **15100**. DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance only and is not a forum for proceedings against employers or commercial entities).*

Please treat this notice with the urgency it deserves.

Yours faithfully,

*(Signed)* 
**[Complainant's Name / Authorized Representative]** 
[Contact Number] 
[Email Address] 

---

### **ANNEXURE INVENTORY (ENCLOSED DOCUMENTS):**
1. Copy of Order Invoice (Rs. 26,999)
2. Delivery receipt dated 14th November 2024
3. Technician inspection job sheet copy dated 21st November 2024
4. Chat screenshots with customer support showing cancellation on 23rd November 2024

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under Section 2(11) and Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, delivering a defective phone and delaying inspection past your return window is a clear deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. I have the technician report confirming hardware fault. I demand an immediate refund or I will escalate to the National Consumer Helpline and e-Daakhil.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre sir/madam, why are you threatening with consumer court and all? Look, our system automatically locks the replacement option after 7 days, no matter what. The technician report is fine, but backend team says policy is policy. Still... since you have the report and you are creating a big issue, let me check with my senior manager... okay, we can offer you a repair or store credit, but full cash refund of Rs. 26,999 is not possible directly. Take the repair na?

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You precisely cited Section 2(11) for deficiency in service and Section 84 for product liability under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, while mentioning concrete proof (technician report) and escalation channels.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Do not accept store credit or forced repairs for a DOA (Dead on Arrival) or manufacturing defect received out-of-the-box. Insist on a complete refund to the original payment source.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Under Section 14 of the Consumer Protection Act, supplying a defective product mandates a full refund of Rs. 26,999 along with compensation; I reject store credit and demand a full cash refund immediately.
